question: a conservative, stable, accurate no-flux scalar wall for advection oblique to the lattice

rig.geometry: doubly periodic oblique channel, slope 1/2, P=50 W=30 box 100x100, D2Q5(2/3)
rig.null_test: uniform C with Poiseuille profile across the channel is a steady state of the continuous problem; any deviation is the wall scheme's

bounce_back.note: conservative; bounded in this 2-D rig with an O(1) wall layer; the SAME wall diverges in 3-D D3Q7 at the pin (results/bifurcation_g4_control.json)

non_equilibrium_reflection.outcome: REFUTED: exact on uniform C + uniform u (machine-zero deviation), but its per-link exchange is proportional to local C - a positive-feedback pump that diverges with any gradient

noble_torczynski.outcome: the best conservative candidate: exact mass, stable (u_w = 0 form), true-wall geometry, wall layer ~20% below bounce-back's; the u_w = local form diverges under plug flow

bouzidi_reflection.outcome: REFUTED on the G4 control (3-D): stable axis-aligned but retains 0.25 of the scalar - the interpolation is not conservative and a scalar has no pressure field to self-correct (results/bifurcation_g4_control.json)

layer_scaling.reading: amp ~ 5 u_lat, decreasing in (tau-1/2) with measured exponent ~ -0.7; at the stability pin refinement at fixed u_lat grows tau-1/2 linearly, so the layer shrinks ~ res^0.7 - a ~1% window bias needs ~48 cells per radius

trt_lambda_sweep.reading: no Lambda cures the layer (wall amp GROWS with Lambda); Lambda = 1/12 minimises the mid-channel spill, 4x below BGK

paths_forward: (a) Noble-Torczynski walls + TRT Lambda=1/12 + high resolution (~48 cells/radius) on HPC - layer budgeted by the measured scaling; needs the NT ADE operator ported to OpenLB

(b) a boundary-layer-corrected wall scheme - open theory: the layer is the equilibrium face-flux inconsistency, no collision knob removes it, and every conservative local correction measured so far either keeps it (BB, NT) or destabilises (NER)
